articles.title: Visions of AI: GPT-3 Moment for Physical AI
articles.content:
### 物理AI与机器人革命：Skild AI的突破

晚安，各位读者。我最近开始尝试一个新的栏目“物理AI展望”，专注于介绍人工智能和新兴科技初创公司。虽然这个栏目的发布频率尚未确定，但世界上有许多令人着迷的初创企业值得我们探讨和分享。这个栏目旨在成为您晚间八点东部时间的轻松阅读。

到2026年底，物理AI和体现AI（即具备身体的AI）的大额融资突然激增，特别是在机器人“大脑”软件和人形机器人领域，这种人形机器人的形态是双足（类似人类）的机器人。虽然尚未确定这一趋势是否具有重大意义或持久性，但它紧随中国多家机器人公司上市之后。中国被广泛视为世界机器人领域的领导者，尤其是在当前销售、硬件和制造方面。

大约三周前，一家名为Skild AI的物理AI初创公司发布了其S1模型，这是一个用于机器人的上下文学习模型。Skild AI在2026年已实现超过1亿美元的收入。该公司声称，S1是一个基础模型，可以通过一次示例（一次性学习）进行学习。他们表示，该模型可以通过一次视频提示，无需微调，就能学习从未见过的10分钟长的任务。

经过深入调查，虽然这是一个由行业推动的营销概念，但我确实认为S1可能成为机器人学习领域的GPT-3时刻，至少在其2027年的版本中。在AI历史上，这大约对应于2020年。生成预训练转换器3（GPT-3）是OpenAI开发的一个具有1750亿参数的里程碑式大型语言模型，其介绍论文于2020年5月20日发表，距离ChatGPT时刻大约3.5年。

这对物理AI和机器人爱好者来说，是一个极其令人兴奋的消息。
articles.summary:
Good Evening,

Visions of AI is a new feature format I’m experimenting with that will amount to a short profile on an AI or emerging tech startup. The cadence of this style of article is unknown as of yet, but there are a lot of fascinating startups I want to discuss and share about.

This is designed to be light evening reading to go out at a time-slot of 8 pm EST.

In late 2026 there’s been a very sudden spike in massive Physical AI and embodied AI funding rounds, especially in the software around the robotic brain, and humanoid robotics, a form factor of bipedal (human-like) robots. While it remains to be seen how significant or enduring this trend is, it follows a flurry of Chinese robotics companies going public. China is widely seen as the robotics leader of the world, especially in current sales, hardware and manufacturing.

About three weeks ago a Physical AI startup called Skild AI released their S1, an in-context learning model for robotics. Skild AI has hit over $100 million1 in revenue already in 2026. The company claims that S1 new is a foundation model that learns from one example (one-shot learning). They said that it can be taught 10-minute long tasks that it has never seen before, from one video prompt without any fine-tuning.

Share

Embodied AI with a Real Revenue Ramp (Skild)

After doing some digging while it’s a marketing idea (being pushed by the industry), I do believe S1 could qualify as the GPT-3 moment for robotics learning, at least in its 2027 iterations. In the history of AI, that would correspond to around 2020. Generative Pre-trained Transformer 3 (GPT-3) was a landmark 175-billion parameter LLM developed by OpenAI where the research paper introducing it was published on May 20th, 2020, about 3.5 years before the ChatGPT moment itself.

This is tremendously exciting for robotics and Physical AI enthusiasts.

articles.title: A Guide to Grok Bot 2026
articles.content:
Good Morning,
It’s been a while since we’ve brought you an AI Guide, see the rest here.
The consumer AI landscape around personal agents is going to be heating up in 2027. I always suspected Anysphere’s Cursor product was going to be a problem for OpenAI. On August 14th, SpaceX completed its acquisition of Cursor for $60 Billion. With Meta pushing products like Muse in B2C, OpenAI’s ChatGPT and its features might be tested on all sides. Even as Chinese model builders test OpenAI’s models on the token share angle. With a crisis of competition and alignment OpenAI has decided to delay its IPO till sometime next year.
Suddenly in the later quarter of 2026 SpaceX AI appears to be gaining some traction with Grok Bot. Grok Bot is an autonomous AI agent platform developed in collaboration with Cursor. It is included directly as part of paid Cursor subscription plans (such as Cursor Pro and Teams).
Grok Bot appears to be taking a niche that would have gone to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Work or ChatGPT Operator. While it’s too soon to say in September, 2026, it’s quite possible Meta Muse and SpaceX AI’s Grok Bot might be products that can take some customers and their time that would have been spent in ChatGPT previously.
I asked for a no nonsense guide on Grok Bot. Jeff is a software professional and writer of The AI-Augmented Engineer to teach people how to use AI to write better code, ship faster, and level up their careers. He writes weekly deep guides on using tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and more to build awesome apps.
Meta's standalone personal AI agent after Billions spent on compute and talent is called Muse and it launched on September 8, 2026, and early indicators show rapid adoption too. Will OpenAI build a “Codex Bot” to compete with Grok Bot? How will they take on Muse? Is ChatGPT Work going to be competitive with Claude Code? OpenAI have too many products and outside of ChatGPT and Codex, not many are well differentiated or have a defined brand. Anthropic’s Claude Cowork is somewhat similar to Grok Bot in that it’s a bit more accessible. Overall since ChatGPT there really hasn’t been a killer B2C AI product, outside of Google Gemini. Now with Gemini 3.8 with Extended Thinking. In a world of multi-agent collaboration, the way we use AI might shift a lot in the next 18 months.
For me, Meta’s Muse and SpaceX’s Grok Bot make chatbots a bit less relevant in that these are about AI as a utility, helper and assistant in accomplishing tasks. They feature agentic capabilities that have:
Isolated Cloud Machines
Tools with asynchronous & background execution
Human-in-the-loop safeguards
Proactive goal orientated assistants
Grok Bot is aided by X user integration and so even if the Grok chatbot was a relative failure compared to ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude - Grok Bot could accelerate SpaceX AI’s Enterprise adoption and Cursor’s real world utility. It remains to be seen what Anthropic and OpenAI come up with in this vertical. Grok Bot was first introduced about a month ago on August 11th that sounds a lot like Meta’s Muse, branded as an AI teammates you can give real work to.
Grok Bot also seems more like a primarily B2C product but with strong B2B support. We’re still seemingly a far way away from the kind of AI companion that is truly capable even four years after ChatGPT first launched which is astounding to me.
Check out the easy to read and detailed guide by Jeff below.
